newsitem.title: USA: U.S. March existing home sales fell 2.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. March existing home sales fell 2.8 pct.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes fell 2.8 percent in March to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.11 million units from a revised 4.23 million units in February, the National Association of Realtors said Friday.
Wall Street economists had forecast March sales of 4.14 million units.
The March sales rate was down 3.3 percent from sales of 4.25 million in March last year.

The group attributed the drop in last month's home sales activity to adverse weather conditions in some parts of the country and to an increase in interest rates.
In a statement, NAR President Russell Booth said the March slowdown indicates that the housing market is "leveling out to a more normal pattern of activity."
The group said it does not anticipate any major swings in interest rates for the remainder of the year.
